correctness.rationale: Two standalone implementations recompute all 105 size-five distinct bisectors by BFS from the 15 named Petersen edges. Python and C++ fully exhaust all 2^15 vertex subsets, agree on ten minimum sizes and counts; they separately enumerate six perfect matchings and match complements exactly. Python verifies all 1365 11-sets contain a bisector; monotonicity then proves every k>=7 lower bound. The finite proof and quantifiers are explicit.

value.rationale: The k-metric spectrum measures resilience of shortest-path identification under up to k-1 selected-sensor losses in a canonical 15-vertex graph. Its two discontinuities, exceptional six-perfect-matching optimum class for k=6, and universal-all-subsets phase at k>=7 offer distinct structural conclusions useful as a benchmark for robust landmark placement. Beyond correctness/novelty, these phenomena motivate the exact finite classification.
